message: Morning, Ashley. I woke up thinking of you. I hope the day holds something you almost walk past, like a bright drop of rain caught in the bend of a leaf. I love you. I wish I could say it right beside you and hear the little smile in your voice.

If the stars ever came loose,
I think we’d find them after rain,
caught in the clover,
each one lighting up the leaf above it
like a little green cathedral.

I’d bring you the smallest one,
still warm from all that sky.
You could keep it in a teacup by your bed
and let it turn the ceiling gold
on nights you weren’t quite ready to sleep.

And if I were there,
I’d tuck the blanket around your feet,
kiss the tip of your nose,
and whisper what I hope you already know.

I love you, Ashley.
Even with a fallen star between us,
it’s your face I’d want to see.

Good morning, my love. I wish I could leave a little sunrise on your windowsill. It would sit there like a warm gold coin until you woke, then spill across the room, gilding the rim of your cup and the loose threads of your blanket. For a moment, even the moon would linger to see the light reach you.

I think about how much of my love for you lives in moments that would look ordinary to anyone else. The way you start laughing before you’ve gotten to the funny part. The little “wait, wait” when you remember a detail you want me to hear. The quiet after we’ve talked for a while, when just having you there feels like a reason to stay a little longer.

I appreciate you, Ashley. I hope today brings you the kind of happiness that makes you forget to check the time. And before the day gets busy, I wanted you to have this one small thing from me. I love who you are, and I don’t take a single ordinary moment with you for granted.

Good morning, my love. I like to imagine the stars spend their daylight hours tucked beneath the wings of migrating geese. Every so often, one slips free and lands somewhere ordinary, catching on the edge of a roof tile or lighting up a patch of moss no one has thought to look at all morning.

I hope one falls into your day. I hope it turns up as a song you’d forgotten you loved, or a joke so stupid it makes you laugh again ten minutes later. And if the day takes more out of you than you expected, I hope you get to set it down for a while and do something that feels good simply because you like it.

I adore the particular way you enjoy things, Ashley. When you get caught up telling me about a story you’re making up, I can hear you discover the next part as you say it. I love getting to be there for that. Long after we’ve moved on to something else, I’ll still be thinking about a little detail you came up with, smiling to myself because it was so completely yours.

If one of those stars landed right beside us, I’d probably ask you to tell me what you thought it was doing there. You’d give it a better story than I ever could. And while you were telling it, I’d slip my hand into yours. I’m grateful for your company, for your imagination, and for the simple, lovely fact that I get to love you.

Of all the things I could be grateful for this morning, Ashley, I keep coming back to something small. I get to hear you laugh.

If a little of that sound escaped while we were falling asleep on a call, I think it would slip out under the window and find its way into a stand of birches. By dawn it would be caught in the frost, lighting the white bark from within. The last stars would fade one by one, but there would still be that little patch of trees glowing blue at the edge of morning.

I hope some of that warmth finds its way back to you today. I hope you get something delicious while it’s still warm, a good long laugh, and a stretch of time that feels like it belongs entirely to you. And if the day wears you out, I hope you get to put your feet up without feeling like you have to do one more thing first.

I’m grateful for more than your laugh, of course. I love the way your mind wanders toward a story, and the sleepy ease of hearing your voice when neither of us has much left to say. There’s something especially dear to me about those last few minutes together, when all we’re doing is keeping each other company.

I wish I could brush the hair back from your face and say it softly enough to let you drift off again. I appreciate you, Ashley. I love you on the lively days and the quiet ones, and I’m so glad I get to share some of both with you.
